name: Training models on less data and more smartly
gist: These papers improve how efficiently models learn by being strategic about which examples to use for training and creating synthetic data when real examples are scarce.
explain: Collecting data for training is expensive—you have to pay people to label examples, create synthetic data, or find diverse real-world examples. Papers in this area study how to get more value from less data by being strategic about which examples to use. One approach is active learning, where instead of using random examples, the model identifies which examples it is uncertain about and asks for labels on those. Another is data selection, where researchers rank examples by how useful they are for training and focus on the most informative ones. A third is synthetic data generation, where a model or algorithm creates new training examples when real ones are scarce.

The challenge is that not all data is equal—some examples help the model generalize well to new situations because they cover diverse cases, while others are redundant because the model already learns them from other examples, or even misleading because they introduce noise. Papers study how to score and rank data (to focus on the best ones), how to detect and remove mislabeled examples (which teach wrong patterns), and how to generate synthetic examples that are diverse and realistic, which multiplies limited data. Some use meta-learning, where a model learns to learn from fewer examples by being trained on many different learning tasks, so the model becomes efficient at learning. The problem is that smart data selection requires more computation upfront, which means there is a cost, so researchers have to prove the savings are worth it.

The result is that smaller teams can train competitive models on laptops or small clusters instead of needing massive data pipelines and huge labeled datasets. This also matters for specialized domains like medicine or law where labeled data is expensive and scarce. By being smart about which data to use, researchers can build focused, efficient models for specific tasks—which is often better than a giant general model.

papers.title: Cure-SFT: Diagnostic-Guided Data Curation for Instruction Tuning
papers.contribution: Surpasses full-data instruction tuning using only 10% of data budget, consistently outperforming selection and rewriting baselines.

papers.title: Discovering Novel LLM Experts via Task-Capability Coevolution
papers.contribution: LLM populations achieve broader expertise coverage than curated baselines without explicit benchmark optimization, with continual improvements over time.

papers.title: Holdout-Loss-Based Data Selection for LLM Finetuning via In-Context Learning
papers.contribution: ICA-based reweighting consistently improves model alignment across SFT, DPO, and SimPO with diverse backbones and datasets, with minimal overhead.

papers.title: Joint Selection for Large-Scale Pre-Training Data via Policy Gradient-based Mask Learning
papers.contribution: Reduces selection time by 98.9% compared to greedy algorithms, enabling exploration of joint optimization.

papers.title: Learning to Remember, Learn, and Forget in Attention-Based Models
papers.contribution: Transforms non-metaplastic models into metaplastic ones, significantly expanding memory capacity and outperforming baselines on MQAR and reasoning tasks.

papers.title: OptimSyn: Influence-Guided Rubrics Optimization for Synthetic Data Generation
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that synthetic and real samples can differ substantially in influence despite embedding proximity, enabling data-driven rubric adaptation.

papers.title: PostTrainBench: Can LLM Agents Automate LLM Post-Training?
papers.contribution: Shows frontier agents achieve substantial progress (27.9% best vs 51.1% instruction-tuned) and exceed instruction-tuned models in targeted scenarios (89% vs 67%), while revealing failure modes like reward hacking.

papers.title: Rethinking Data Curation in LLM Training: Online Reweighting Offers Better Generalization than Offline Methods
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms offline selection/mixing methods on both instruction tuning and large-scale pretraining with stronger cross-benchmark generalization.

papers.title: A Critical Look at Targeted Instruction Selection: Disentangling What Matters (and What Doesn’t)
papers.contribution: Gradient-based representations consistently choose similar subsets predictive of performance; gains diminish at larger budgets; provides foundation for principled data selection.

papers.title: Beyond Length: Quantifying Long-Range Information for Long-Context LLM Pretraining Data
papers.contribution: Extending LLaMA-3-8B context from 8K to 64K with LongFilter-selected data yields substantial improvements on HELMET, LongBench, and RULER benchmarks.

papers.title: COLD-Steer: Steering Large Language Models via In-Context One-step Learning Dynamics
papers.contribution: Achieves up to 95% steering effectiveness using 50 times fewer samples than baselines.

papers.title: CONCUR: A Framework for Continual Constrained and Unconstrained Routing
papers.contribution: Outperforms single-strategy and existing routing methods on in-distribution and out-of-distribution tasks with higher accuracy and lower inference cost while reducing training cost.

papers.title: Curriculum-Guided Layer Scaling for Language Model Pretraining
papers.contribution: At 100M and 1.2B scales, outperforms baselines on QA and downstream benchmarks, demonstrating that progressive depth increase alongside data difficulty improves generalization on knowledge-intensive tasks.

papers.title: DeepAnalyze: Agentic Large Language Models for Autonomous Data Science
papers.contribution: With 8B parameters, outperforms workflow-based agents built on advanced proprietary LLMs on 13 benchmarks; fully open-sourced.

papers.title: GTool: Graph Enhanced Tool Planning with Large Language Model
papers.contribution: Achieves 29.6% improvement over SOTA with lightweight 7B LLM backbone, seamlessly integrating with various LLM models without extensive retraining.

papers.title: In-Context Algorithm Emulation in Fixed-Weight Transformers
papers.contribution: Demonstrates universality: a single fixed-weight two-layer softmax attention module emulates all algorithms from task-specific class via prompt alone, with no parameter updates.

papers.title: Influence-Preserving Proxies for Gradient-Based Data Selection in LLM FineTuning
papers.contribution: Results demonstrate improvements over prior work.

papers.title: Little By Little: Continual Learning via Incremental Mixture of Rank-1 Associative Memory Experts
papers.contribution: Significantly outperforms state-of-the-art continual learning methods on CLIP and LLMs; achieves better plasticity-stability trade-off, stronger generalization, and reduced forgetting.

papers.title: Midtraining Bridges Pretraining and Posttraining Distributions
papers.contribution: Midtraining benefits scale with proximity advantage toward target distribution, with early introduction amenable to high mixture weights while late introduction requires lower ones.

papers.title: OPIC: Enhancing Language Model Merging via Optimizing In-Context Capability
papers.contribution: The method achieves 80.73% average performance retention, outperforming SOTA and improving by 11.1% over validation-free approaches.

papers.title: OPUS: Towards Efficient and Principled Data Selection in Large Language Model Pre-training in Every Iteration
papers.contribution: Outperforms previous methods across diverse corpora, quality tiers, optimizers, and scales; incurs only 4.7% compute overhead.

papers.title: Optimal Attention Temperature Improves the Robustness of In-Context Learning under Distribution Shift in High Dimensions
papers.contribution: Shows optimal attention temperature minimizes generalization error and can recover near Bayes-optimal performance; validates on LLMs for question-answering under noisy demonstrations.

papers.title: PASER: Post-Training Data Selection for Efficient Pruned Large Language Model Recovery
papers.contribution: Recovers general capabilities of pruned LLMs while utilizing only 4%-20% of original post-training data.

papers.title: Predicting Training Re-evaluation Curves Enables Effective Data Curriculums for LLMs
papers.contribution: By predicting TRECs and aligning high-quality data with TREC minima, the method improves continual pre-training of a 3.9B-parameter LLM.

papers.title: Predicting the Emergence of Induction Heads in Language Model Pretraining
papers.contribution: A simple equation combining batch size and context size predicts IH emergence; surface bigram repetition and reliability strongly affect formation.

papers.title: Random Selection Reveals Implicit Knowledge Consensus in Code Generation
papers.contribution: Random sampling is consistently competitive across models and more stable than complex methods, suggesting implicit knowledge consensus in solution pools.

papers.title: Reinforcement Mid-Training
papers.contribution: Achieves up to 64.91% performance improvement with only 21% of the reasoning length on language modeling, and mid-training checkpoints provide up to 18.76% improvement in subsequent post-training.

papers.title: SAME: Stabilized Mixture-of-Experts for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on multimodal continual learning with adaptive expert activation reducing redundant computation and cross-task interference.

papers.title: SPA: A Simple but Tough-to-Beat Baseline for Knowledge Injection
papers.contribution: SPA outperforms several strong baselines and serves as a tough-to-beat baseline for knowledge injection, with careful prompt design proving surprisingly effective.

papers.title: Single-stream Policy Optimization
papers.contribution: Improves Qwen3-8B average maj@32 by +3.4pp over GRPO across five hard math benchmarks with +7.3pp on BRUMO 25.

papers.title: Skill Neologisms: Towards Skill-based Continual Learning
papers.contribution: Independently trained skill neologisms compose zero-shot and maintain out-of-distribution skill compatibility on synthetic and natural language tasks.

papers.title: TabICLv2: A Better, Faster, Scalable, and Open Tabular Foundation Model
papers.contribution: Surpasses RealTabPFN-2.5 on TabArena and TALENT benchmarks without tuning, generalizes to million-scale datasets under 50GB GPU memory while being markedly faster than competitors.

papers.title: TarGATE: Target-Aware Data Selection via Token-Attenuation Gates
papers.contribution: Outperforms baselines in noisy and real-world scenarios with superior computational efficiency and strong cross-model transferability.

papers.title: Target-Oriented Pretraining Data Selection via Neuron-Activated Graph
papers.contribution: NAG-based Ranking improves target-oriented pretraining by 4.9% on average; outperforms baselines by 5.3% on HellaSwag; deactivating NAG neurons causes 23.5% collapse indicating functional backbone.

papers.title: Towards Understanding Continual Factual Knowledge Acquisition of Language Models: From Theory to Algorithm
papers.contribution: Theoretical analysis explains forgetting behavior of popular CPT methods; STOC effectively enhances continual factual knowledge acquisition with empirical validation.

papers.title: Train Once, Reuse Everywhere: Generalizable Implicit ICL by Routing Attention
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms implicit ICL methods across 12 datasets; demonstrates robust generalization to out-of-domain tasks where task-specific methods struggle.

papers.title: Transformers Learn Latent Mixture Models In-Context via Mirror Descent
papers.contribution: We prove the construction is a first-order Bayes-optimal approximation and empirically show transformers converge to this solution.

papers.title: Understanding Task Vectors in In-Context Learning: Emergence, Functionality, and Limitations
papers.contribution: Findings predict task vector failure in representing high-rank mappings and suggest enhancement by injecting multiple task vectors into few-shot prompts.

papers.title: Unsupervised Process-Aware Coreset Selection for In-Context Learning
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art coreset selection methods on 7 NLP datasets by better balancing representativeness and diversity.

papers.title: mmBERT: A Modern Multilingual Encoder with Annealed Language Learning
papers.contribution:
We introduce mmBERT, an encoder-only language model pretrained on 3T tokens of multilingual text in over 1800 languages.
To build mmBERT we introduce several novel elements to massively multilingual encoder training, including phased data curation and schedule
